lines.text: We held a council of war in the back room of the worst inn in Aldcrown. Six people, one wolfhound, and a great many bad ideas.
Don't touch it.
Refusing the King's Stone is treason. Every lord in the Compact would hang.
Shoot Vance.
Also treason.
Worth it.
Bribe the men who carry the Stone. Swap it for the old one. I know a man who knows a man.
The Stone is guarded by Hounds, day and night. I checked.
I sat with my hands round a cup of hot wine that never warmed them, and thought about water. You can't stop a spring. But you can dig it a channel.
Ilse. The Stone drinks whatever is in me at the moment I touch it. So what if, at that moment, everything I have is somewhere else?
You'd have to pour it all out. All of it. Into one bond, the instant you touch the Stone. And keep pouring, for as long as your hand is on it.
A Tide. But aimed, at one thread. Nobody has ever written down how to do that.
Pour it into me.
It would burst you like a wineskin, Wren. A person has walls. Your Vessel can only stretch so far, so fast.
Then something heavy leaned against my legs. Something that had been drinking from me since the day I named him.
...Ash. Of course. You poured a whole naming into him in one night, and he only got bigger. If anything alive can hold you, it's him.
They'll never let a dog into the cathedral.
I had taken one book from my father's library. The old rite of the Measuring. I'd read it twice on the barge, because Corvin snores.
A lord comes before the Stone with his sword, his seal and his hound. It's Aldric's own rite. Nobody has brought a hound in a hundred years. But nobody ever changed the words.
My lord, that is the most beautiful piece of law I have ever heard.
Ash lifted his head at the sound of his name. His tail thumped the floor, twice.
Six days to teach a wolfhound to hold a spring. And in his whole life, he had never once sat when he was told.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter seventy-six, coming soon.
